$comment: POSIX `environ` — the SMOKE TEST that reading the environment through the shipped `environ` -> `__environ` macro/symbol split WORKS in a DSS-built ELF exec on both arches, debug and release. ★★ READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING WHAT IT PROVES, BECAUSE IT ONCE PROVED LESS THAN IT CLAIMED: this program is a SELF-LOOP and CANNOT witness an OBJECT-IDENTITY property. It reads `environ` through the DSS macro and cross-checks against libc's own `getenv`, but under the ELF COPY RELOCATION binding that shipped at the time BOTH reads went through the very name the exec CLAIMED, so it compared the exec's copy WITH ITSELF — structurally unable to fail. It stayed GREEN on all four legs across the entire window in which a third-party libtcl8.6.so reading the UN-PREFIXED `environ` got NULL and SIGSEGV'd in TclSetupEnv+0xe8 (regression pair `09e1608a` green -> `6f4aab73` rc=139, introduced by `64ee3a16`). ★★★ THE GENERAL RULE that came out of it: AN OBJECT-IDENTITY PROPERTY CANNOT BE WITNESSED BY ONE IMAGE — a test asserting that a symbol denotes the SAME OBJECT must involve a SECOND image DSS did not build. That witness is examples/c-subset/environ_alias_object_identity, which dlopens a gcc-built `.so` reading the un-prefixed name, asserts the VALUE it sees (never mere survival), asserts dlsym SAME_OBJECT=YES on both spellings, and verifies the shipped `.so` itself really relocates against `environ` before trusting it. ⇒ THIS example is kept for what it DOES witness — a live, well-formed environment vector reachable through the shipped descriptor on both ELF arches, debug and release — and NOT for object identity (D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET). BINDING MODEL: every ELF format declares dataImportBinding:got-indirect — the exec reserves a GOT slot per imported object, emits one R_*_GLOB_DAT against it, ld.so writes the LIBRARY object's ADDRESS into the slot at load, and the shared GotIndirect lowering (lea-of-slot + deref) reads it; the exec DEFINES NOTHING (its data-import dynsym rows stay UNDEF, st_size 0). The copy-relocation alternative is DELETED from the vocabulary. WHY `environ` RATHER THAN main's third parameter: POSIX.1 does not specify that parameter at all, so `extern char **environ;` (glibc /usr/include/unistd.h) is the interface portable code actually uses. WHY THE SYMBOL IS `__environ`: glibc declares it UNCONDITIONALLY and exports it STRONG, while `environ` is behind #ifdef __USE_GNU and exported WEAK, and DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every declared name — so the always-present spelling is the safe one. ⓘ That is a SAFETY preference, no longer a CORRECTNESS requirement: under got-indirect ld.so resolves either spelling to glibc's ONE object. It WAS a correctness requirement under copy relocation, which is history worth keeping rather than a live claim. EAGER-IMPORT SAFE, MEASURED before the row shipped on both run legs and two concurring instruments: glibc exports all three spellings at ONE address — `__environ` STRONG (`B`/`g`), `environ`/`_environ` WEAK (`V`/`w`) — 0x20ad58 @GLIBC_2.2.5 (x86_64) and 0x1b7288 @GLIBC_2.17 (aarch64), `nm -D` and `objdump -T` concurring with `DO .bss` SIZE 8. ⚠ the `@@GLIBC_x.y` suffix makes a grep anchored on `$` report a FALSE ABSENT. THE ENVIRONMENT'S CONTENT IS NEVER ASSERTED (it is host-dependent) — only its STRUCTURE plus an agreement check, so the stdout pin is host-independent: every entry must be NAME=VALUE with a non-empty NAME (exit 2/3 — a binding one indirection off, the got-indirect-WITHOUT-deref class, fails the '=' scan on garbage rather than appearing to pass), the vector must be non-empty (exit 4), and environ[0]'s NAME is looked up through libc's OWN getenv with the value required BYTE-IDENTICAL to the text after '=' (exit 7 = getenv cannot see a variable environ claims exists; exit 8 = they disagree). ⚠ THAT AGREEMENT CHECK IS THE SELF-LOOP HALF: getenv reads libc's internal `__environ`, the same object this program reads, so it detects a garbage or stale pointer but NEVER a split. ELF-ONLY, both exclusions deliberate: ✔MEASURED, NEITHER Windows CRT exports `environ` — `objdump -p` plus a direct PE export-directory parse find no `environ`/`_environ`/`__environ` in ucrtbase.dll (2,484 exports) and only the UNDERSCORED `_environ` data export (ordinal 270) in msvcrt.dll (1,330), so a pe arm would have to be a MACRO onto UCRT's `__p__environ` accessor (ordinal 87) and cannot live in unistd.json at all (that descriptor is [elf,macho] — there is no <unistd.h> on pe); macho is DEFERRED because its export could not be measured this cycle and this directory's rule is need-driven + measured, never inferred (the fileno/popen-pclose staging precedent) — an inferred row risks EVERY macho binary's LOAD. Both stay honest S0001. exec-only, not pie: the canonical elf data-object witness (stdio_stream_objects) is likewise exec-only, and this defect was the EXEC arm's. RED-ON-DISABLE: un-ship the row -> S0001; un-ship the macro -> S0001 `got environ`; drop dataImportBinding from the elf exec format -> K_FormatLacksImportSupport at link; neuter the got-indirect deref (a bare lea) -> the vector walk reads the slot's own address as environ[0] and fails the '=' scan at exit 2. ⓘ NOT red-on-disable here any more, and that is exactly why the sibling example exists: repointing the row at the WEAK `environ` spelling now WORKS (ld.so resolves it to the same object), where under copy relocation it returned 1 with no diagnostic. Cross-checked in WSL against `gcc -std=gnu17 -no-pie` (exit 42, identical stdout) — gnu17 rather than c17 because glibc gates the `environ` spelling behind __USE_GNU.
